cohort: 3,179 adolescents aged 11 years from the 2004 Pelotas (Brazil) Birth Cohort Study
finding: The mean sleep duration of the adolescents was 9.3 hours, and longer sleep duration was associated with lower socioeconomic status at birth, lower mother's education level, being female, not being born via cesarean section, not having classes in the morning shift, and higher levels of physical activity.
mod_finding: Shorter sleep duration was associated with cesarean section delivery.
